correctness.rationale: The Parseval Gram condition on three consecutive spatial sites is exactly ∑w=1, ∑wz=0 and ∑wz²=0. Three positive frequencies must form a 3×3 unitary Vandermonde matrix, hence equal 1/3 weights on a coset of the cubic subgroup, existing only if 3|N. If four distinct frequencies existed for gcd(N,6)=1, a missing quadratic coefficient in the vanishing polynomial for the generalized 4×4 Vandermonde rows would force ∑_{i<j} z_i z_j=0, a length-six vanishing sum of N-th roots. Read the original Lam–Leung Theorem 5.2 in full, verifying allowed lengths are additive semigroup of prime divisors, so 6 is excluded when gcd(N,6)=1. For even 3∤N, the explicit 4-node construction k=⌊N/4⌋ and positive symmetric weights satisfies first and second moments exactly. For gcd(N,6)=1, Carathéodory applied to origin in convex hull of 4-real-dimensional two-moment embedding yields ≤5 nodes; the lower bound forces 5. Vandermonde/Lagrange coefficient extraction gives unique real weights on each fixed 5-node support and an exact strict-positivity test. Independently checked constructed even rules and small cases, but finite numerical examples are not the all-N proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Lam–Leung gives only obstruction lengths for root sums, not positivity/constructive minimal frame count. Dutkay–Ranasinghe constructs Parseval frames for self-affine measures using iterated systems, not the finite cyclic {0,1,2} minimum and support positivity. Frederick–Mayeli concerns frame spectral pairs for unions of domains and general Riesz spectra; the published antipodal-triplet six-frequency statement concerns different spatial sites.

The combination of independent lower bounds, explicit construction, and Carathéodory is needed.

It contrasts with the larger unweighted prime-order sample requirement and supplies constructive sparse quadrature.
